chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked
about hunting fish, and if he has not named (Bismillah) over it, so he said: There is no problem with it, if it is alive that he seizes it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to recite Bismillah when catching fish in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the recitation of Bismillah is not a strict condition for the permissibility of fishing, distinguishing this from terrestrial hunting where it is often emphasized. The ruling hinges on the fish being alive at the moment of capture, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the act of extraction itself suffices for halal status in aquatic creatures. This hadith is foundational in establishing the ease of obtaining seafood in Islamic dietary law.
